groups.contentHtml:
21. It brings teaching problems when based on old methods.
22. Students should be cautious about applying for an online course.
23. Computer can be applied to certain courses.
24. The opinion about personal contact is not helpful.
25. Online course comes with technological development.
26. Online course should have more time flexibility.

analyses.content: 彼得明确表示是时候彻底改变旧的教学方式了，这说明他同意旧方法会带来问题。
你可能会因为林恩在录音中提到了“traditional methods”就误选了她，但她其实是在维护传统教学，并没有说它有问题。

When I read that article, it was clear to me that Professor Smith does not favor the traditional methods of classroom teaching. Although I can certainly acknowledge that there are some advantages to online course, I would say that internet courses are not always the best means for teaching and learning. I think it's about time to revolutionize the old teaching style, though.
林恩明确提出，希望学生在报名线上课程前好好考虑一下它的负面影响，这也就是提醒他们要保持谨慎。
你可能没听出来“考虑负面影响（consider the negatives）”和题目里的“谨慎（cautious）”是一个意思，另外紧跟着彼得就说这不是什么大问题，从而排除了彼得也同意的可能。
But I would hope that students consider the negatives of online learning before enrolling in online courses. This shouldn't be a big issue since online courses are so common these days.
彼得引述教授的观点说电脑学习非常适合某些课程，特别是技术类课程。
听完彼得的话你可能会以为两人都同意，但后面林恩立刻接了一句“这个理论对我不适用（doesn't work for me）”，所以只有彼得同意。
And Professor Smith points out that computer learning is well-suited for some courses, especially the technical courses. Unfortunately, that theory doesn't work for me.
彼得直截了当地说，传统教学里的个人互动被高估了，没多大价值，就是个让人分心的东西。
你可能会觉得录音里的“personal interaction”没有精确对应题目上的“personal contact”而犹豫，或者没听到紧接着林恩用一句强烈的“我坚决不同意（I disagree strongly）”反驳了他。

Anyway, next part is personal interaction. I think the personal interaction offered by traditional teaching is overrated in the article and doesn't have much value. I think it's a distraction and that time could be better spent on the subject matter of the course. Oh, I disagree strongly, Peter. You're dismissing the benefits of face-to-face interaction between students and teachers in traditional classroom settings.
彼得指出在线课程能培养学生的技术能力，林恩马上回复了一句完全同意。
你可能不知道“I can't agree more（我不能同意更多了）”其实是表示“极度赞同”的意思，从而漏掉了林恩的态度，误选单人。

I'm still not sure about that, but online courses can foster students' technological skills. In learning the subject matter online, students will gain the technical know-how they'll need in their future endeavors. I can't agree more.
林恩先抛出关于在线课程时间灵活性的疑问，彼得解释说这点极其重要，能让时间不固定的人来学习，随后林恩也明确说了同意。
两人一问一答，你可能注意力全放在了彼得的大段解释上，却没注意到林恩最后用来确认态度的简短句“I agree”。

What do you think Professor Smith means when he says online courses should be flexible in time? That's essential. The point of learning online is to allow those who can't attend courses at fixed time. I agree.

questions.question: What does Professor Smith think of the usage of the Internet on campus?

analyses.content: 彼得解释说教授想表达的是，学生们早就习惯在网上做研究了，这完全对应选项A里的“严重依赖互联网”。
后面提到了许多老师正在教学生把电脑当做研究工具，你如果光听见这句可能会误选C，但实际上这是在描述现状，而不是教授提出的建议。

The second part of the article shares some thoughts about the use of internet on campus. I'm kind of lost in that part. Well, I think what he's trying to say is that students are already accustomed to doing their research on the internet. Although some people say computers could be better used for other purposes, he emphasizes that many teachers are already instructing students to use the computer as a research tool.

options.optionContent: Students are encouraged to use other useful resources.

questions.question: What's the meaning of Professor Smith's term "divided"?

analyses.content: 录音直接解释了“divided”的意思，即并不是所有的学生都能轻易地接触和购买到电脑。
录音里提到有人“害怕使用电脑（afraid to use）”，但这前面紧跟着个否定的“certainly not”，如果你没听到这个否定短语，非常容易掉进陷阱选A。

What about the next part saying that students are divided? Do you know what that means? Well, it's certainly not that some students are afraid to use computers. They're already well accustomed to that. You're right about that. Most students already use the internet as their primary source for news and information. Professor Smith probably intends to say that computers are not easily accessible and available to all students. Yes, not all students can afford computers.

questions.question: What kind of help does Professor Smith think students should get?

analyses.content: 录音里明说，有了在线课程后，学生能够在线（online）获取到他们需要的任何信息。
录音里同时出现了同学（fellow students）和教授（professor），但它们前面有个关键短语“Instead of（而不是去问...）”，如果你没捕捉到这个表示排除的词，就极其容易选错A或C。

And as Professor Smith note, with online courses, the student support system is already in place. Instead of asking fellow students or the professor for assistance, students would be able to get any information they need online, and this assistance would be available immediately.

questions.question: What is Professor Smith's view on the purpose of introducing the computers in school?

analyses.content: 林恩直接点破了教授推广在线课程的真实目的，就是觉得这能让学校赚更多的钱（make more money），完美对应C选项的盈利（make profit）。
彼得在提问的时候猜测是不是为了“减少费用（reducing some of the fees）”，但紧接着就被林恩的话否定了。如果你只听到彼得的猜测就急着选B，就会完美错过正确答案。

So why do you think Professor Smith is recommending the use of computers as the school's main means of educating students? Do you think he is interested in reducing some of the fees associated with traditional classroom courses? I think it's all about the money. He is promoting online courses simply because he thinks it will enable the school to make more money.
